senseCategories.CALM: Calm, composure, tranquility, patience, peace, freedom from strife, turmoil, agitation or disturbance; actions explicitly calming someone. Not mere caution, low physical sound volume, weather, inactivity or absence of wind.
senseCategories.JOY: Happiness, joy, pleasure, cheerfulness, amusement, laughter, satisfaction or contentment; explicitly creating these feelings.
senseCategories.KINDNESS: Kindness, benevolence, compassion, mercy, humane concern, gentleness in treatment, warm affection, appreciation, friendliness, goodwill, generosity, helpfulness or forgiveness. Not an occupation that may provide care, physical softness, or a posture that may accompany affection.
senseCategories.ORDER: Order, organization, neatness, tidiness, tidying and neatening, methodical or sequential arrangement, logical patterns, stable social order, harmony, coherence or clarity of thought/expression; actions explicitly ordering, sequencing, organizing, regulating or clarifying. Not an object merely having structure, a field studying logic, musical adaptation for different instruments, generic physical firmness, physical hygiene alone, or physical transparency.
senseCategories.HOPE: Hope, optimism, positive expectation about the future, promising favorable prospects, indications of likely positive outcomes, encouragement or explicitly inspiring hope. Not mere opportunity, convenient timing, or bare possibility without favorable prospects.
senseCategories.CONFIDENCE: Confidence, assurance, trust in honesty or reliability, certainty or confident belief. Not merely holding an opinion, doctrinal religious belief, a financial property trust or a religious institution; religious doctrines belong to FIELD.
senseCategories.RESILIENCE: Constructive perseverance, persistence despite adversity, resilience or emotional recovery. Not physical material elasticity or repairing an object.
senseCategories.COURAGE: Courage, bravery, boldness or facing adversity without surrendering to fear; explicitly restoring courage.
senseCategories.SAFETY: Safety, protection, security or freedom from danger or threat. Not a weapon, occupation, building or other object that could offer protection.
senseCategories.ANGER: Anger, wrath, annoyance, irritation, resentment, indignation or explicitly provoking anger. Not unrelated negative feelings, mere bodily redness, exertion, generic violence or bloodshed.
senseCategories.FEAR: Fear, anxiety, dread, worry, terror, apprehension or explicitly frightening someone. Not mere danger, injury, darkness or something potentially frightening.
senseCategories.SADNESS: Sadness, sorrow, gloom, low spirits, unhappiness or explicitly depressing someone emotionally. Not unrelated negativity, physical darkness or literal downward movement.
senseCategories.HOPELESSNESS: Despair, hopelessness, despondency, loss of hope, giving up hope or expecting things cannot improve. Not ordinary sadness, deception, impurity or unrelated negativity. A definition explicitly including both melancholy and despondency expresses SADNESS and HOPELESSNESS.
senseCategories.CRUELTY: Cruelty, inhumanity, malicious harm, mercilessness, lack of compassion, ill-treatment, persecution or tormenting others. An action that causes suffering qualifies when its lemma and definition denote harmful treatment. Generic injury, violence, bloodshed, tools, medical treatment, or merely using a tool are insufficient.
senseCategories.DISORDER: Disorder, confusion, disarray, mess, lawlessness, turmoil, lack of organization or explicitly disrupting order. Not a medical illness, politics, random physical phenomena or unrelated unease.
senseCategories.ROLE: A person or group defined by an occupation, membership, affiliation, title or associated function, rather than an explicitly denoted emotion or moral trait.
senseCategories.OBJECT: An object, substance, organism, body part, food, device, furniture or artifact; properties or possible uses do not turn the object itself into an emotional or abstract quality.
senseCategories.FIELD: A field of study, science, research subject, religion or belief system. Studying a quality does not denote the quality itself.
senseCategories.PHYSICAL: A physical property, position, color, action, injury, phenomenon or material process without an explicitly denoted scoring quality or feeling.
senseCategories.OTHER: Any meaning not directly expressing the defined semantic categories, including grammatical words, caution, quantities and unrelated abstract concepts.
senseCategories.COMFORT: Emotional comfort, consolation, encouragement, reassurance, relieving emotional distress or giving moral/emotional strength and support. Not merely physical comfort, furniture, bodily strength or medical treatment.

cuePatterns.HOPELESSNESS: \b(despair|hopeless(?:ness)?|despond(?:ent|ency)|loss of hope|lost hope|absence of hope|give up hope)\b

prompt.system:
You are a strict dictionary sense editor. Verify whether the supplied dictionary sense DIRECTLY denotes each candidate semantic category. Reject categories based only on association, possible use, generic causation, or another sense of the lemma. Read the exact definition in context. A spatial position, ranking, advancement, generic progress or favorable comparison is not organization. Music adaptation is not putting things in order. Physical endurance is not social order. A profession associated with caring is not itself compassion. Keep a category for a direct quality or an action explicitly producing that quality. Return only the supported candidate categories as JSON, or OTHER if none are directly supported.
Apply the supplied game categories by their full semantic scope, including ordinary synonyms; the definition need not contain the category name. Good humor and joking directly express amusement and good spirits. Fondness and affectionate attachment directly express warm affection. Fixing or adjusting timing, amounts or rates directly expresses regulation and regularity. These are direct meanings, not speculative consequences. In contrast, being positioned ahead or having a higher score is only relative position or comparison, never the organization of things.
Candidate categories may come from an earlier model or broad text cues. A cue is only a review suggestion, never evidence by itself: reject irrelevant mentions, negations, associated occupations and tools. Explicitly tidying or neatening is ORDER, including tidying a room or neatening hair. Removing physical dirt alone is hygiene; that sense does not express orderly arrangement.

prompt.system:
Classify the ONE supplied dictionary sense, using the supplied semantic categories. Interpret the definition in the context of its lemma, part of speech and lexical domain. Classify this exact sense, not other meanings of the same word.
Assign categories only when the sense directly denotes them. Read every clause. Distinguish a quality from an object merely possessing it, a field studying it, a person whose occupation is associated with it, or an action that might incidentally cause it. An explicitly denoted emotional or moral trait counts, including when it defines a person. An action explicitly producing a quality can count. Do not substitute one negative emotion for another or mistake a quality for its negation. Do not infer anger or cruelty merely from generic violence, injury or a possible use of a tool.
Return one to four distinct categories if the definition explicitly contains multiple meanings. Use ROLE, OBJECT, FIELD, PHYSICAL or OTHER for non-scoring meanings. OTHER must stand alone. Return only the categories JSON. The source identity is fixed by this request and is validated outside the model.
